settings.tagline: Empowering Families. Strengthening Communities. Creating Sustainable Futures.

posts.title: Breaking Barriers: How 10 Young Girls with Disabilities Mastered Coding in Kano
posts.author: Malam Ibrahim Al-Hassan
posts.excerpt: Inside the landmark Holiday Digital Skills Boot Camp funded directly by BHB in collaboration with The Ability First Tech Hub.
posts.content:
In a world increasingly shaped by digital technology, persons with disabilities in Northern Nigeria face disproportionate barriers in education and economic participation.

To bridge this critical divide, BHB Family Support and Development Foundation partnered with The Ability First Tech Hub to deliver an intensive, high-impact Holiday Digital Skills Boot Camp for adolescent girls in Kano Metropolitan.

Over several weeks of intensive hands-on instruction, 10 young participants—living with visual impairments, hearing difficulties, and physical mobility challenges—mastered computer architecture fundamentals, accessible screen-reader navigation (NVDA and JAWS), HTML/CSS coding logic, and assistive tools.

"Before this boot camp, I believed computer coding was something closed off to someone who is blind," shared 15-year-old Halima, one of the cohort participants. "Today, I built my own digital profile and learned how software can be made accessible to everyone."

Every graduate received a specialized assistive laptop and ongoing mentorship from our technical team. BHB Foundation is currently finalizing plans to expand this programme to 50 additional girls across neighboring Local Government Areas in early 2027.

posts.title: Community-Led Infrastructure: How One Settlement Restored Its Clean Water Source
posts.author: Engr. Usman Farouk
posts.excerpt: Rather than providing temporary external fixes, BHB helped establish a local Water Committee that manages borehole maintenance independently.
posts.content:
When a primary borehole pump broke down in a suburban settlement outside Kano, over 800 households faced severe shortages, forcing women and children to walk miles for water.

Rejecting top-down charitable fixes that fail once funding ends, BHB Foundation facilitated an open town hall uniting neighborhood elders, youth leaders, and local mechanics.

Together, residents formed a 7-member Water Management Committee, established a community maintenance fund with modest monthly contributions, and repaired the solar-powered pump. Today, the borehole operates continuously, managed entirely by the neighborhood.

comments.postTitle: Breaking Barriers: How 10 Young Girls with Disabilities Mastered Coding in Kano
comments.content: This is a truly transformative initiative for Kano State. Digital literacy for adolescent girls with disabilities addresses one of the most overlooked sectors of inclusive development.

team.name: Hauwa Musa Shehu
team.bio:
Experience & Contribution: Experienced in managing empowerment programmes and coordinating field activities, with previous roles as Program Manager, Field Supervisor, and Field Assistant. These experiences have strengthened my commitment to developing practical, sustainable initiatives that create opportunities and improve lives.

Passion & Commitment: Passionate about empowering individuals, supporting vulnerable communities, and creating sustainable opportunities that enable people to achieve dignity, independence, and a better quality of life.

team.name: Zango S Habibu
team.bio:
Experienced in managing business operations and supporting community-based empowerment, education, healthcare, and social development initiatives.

Committed to empowering individuals and families, supporting vulnerable communities, and contributing to sustainable social development through the mission of BHB Foundation.

team.name: Fatima Ibrahim Musa
team.bio: Fatima is a lawyer, development specialist, and social justice advocate with over a decade of experience in justice reform, gender inclusion, and human rights advocacy. She is the Founder and Executive Director of Refined Hearts Foundation and has worked with organizations including PPDC, the British Council, and NRC. At BHB Foundation, she brings her expertise to advancing welfare support, skills development, and community-led initiatives that improve lives.

team.name: Dr. Aminatu Kwaku Chiroma
team.bio: An academic and public health expert with over a decade of experience across maternal and child health, immunization, and health systems strengthening. She serves as a Co-Investigator on Gates Foundation-funded projects and is a Consultant Lecturer at Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital and Bayero University Kano.

team.name: Halima Abubakar
team.bio: A development leader with 18+ years of experience overseeing major donor-funded portfolios across West Africa, including a $150M USAID program. She specializes in civil society capacity building, peacebuilding, and advancing policy protections for women and youth.

team.name: Hafsat Yusuf Haruna
team.bio: Hafsat Yusuf Haruna is a programme management professional with experience in project implementation, administration, community engagement and programme coordination. She supports BHB Foundation in ensuring that programmes are effectively coordinated, implemented and aligned with the Foundation’s mission and goals.

team.name: Isa Babale
team.bio: Isa Babale is a Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning professional with extensive experience in programme evaluation, data analysis, performance monitoring and evidence-based decision-making. He supports BHB in strengthening programme quality, accountability, learning and the measurement of impact.
